newsitem.title: UK: Former British minister suffers breakdown.
newsitem.headline: Former British minister suffers breakdown.

text.p: Former British government minister Allan Stewart, who has resigned as an election candidate, was taken to hospital on Thursday after suffering a nervous breakdown, Conservative Party officials said.

Stewart, 54, a former Scottish Office minister, agreed to stand down on Tuesday after press reports linked him to a married woman he is said to have met while attending a clinic specialising in alcohol problems.

Stewart's Eastwood constituency in Glasgow is the Conservatives' safest seat in Scotland and the party has been struggling to limit the damage caused by his resignation so close to the general election due to be held on May 1.
Conservative Party Central Office said Stewart had felt the strain of recent events and wished him a quick recovery.
Stewart was a junior minister in the Scottish Office until 1995, when he resigned that post after a court appearance for a pick-axe confrontation with roads protesters.
